risk_name.description: A short yet descriptive title of the risk. Someone reading just the name should be able to grasp the nature of the risk.
examples: cyber security
infrastructure
financial sustainability
climate change

description.description: A concise explanation of what the risk entails, taken from the report. If the text does not provide such information, output null.
examples: Significant price fluctuations in equity markets due to macroeconomic shifts.
Unauthorized access to customer data via phishing attacks.

driver.description: List of dictionaries where each dictionary has the driver name as key and driver description as value. Use null if not available in source.

items.description: Dictionary with driver name as key and description as value. Keys and values are both optional.

.*.description: Driver description or null if no description available

examples.Interest Rate Hikes: Regular increases in central bank rates reduce market liquidity

examples.Weak Password Policies: Simple passwords are easily cracked by automated tools

recommendations.description: Actions suggested to mitigate the risk. Include ALL recommendations found in source.

examples: Implement stop-loss orders at 5% intervals.
Enforce multifactor authentication for all user accounts.
Establish backup supplier relationships in different geographic regions.

trend.description: How the risk has evolved or is projected to change, with quantifiable data when available.
examples: Increasing year-over-year - ranked #3 last year, now #1
Stable since 2020 with consistent 15% occurrence rate
Declining due to improved regulatory frameworks

likelihood.description: Probability information as stated in source - can be qualitative or quantitative.
examples: High
15% probability over next 12 months
Increasing frequency - up 40% from last year
Low but rising due to new threat vectors

impact.description: Potential severity, consequences, and magnitude if risk materializes, including any scoring information.
examples: Up to $10M in losses with 6-month recovery period
Regulatory fines up to $5M plus reputational damage
Rated 8 out of 10 on severity scale by industry experts
Operational disruption affecting 70% of customer base

risk_indicator.description: Specific quantifiable metric used to track the risk (exclude survey-based metrics).
examples: Value at Risk (VaR)
Number of critical incidents per quarter
System uptime percentage
Credit default ratio

events.description: Specific real-world incidents mentioned in source with concrete details.

examples: March 2024 flash crash - S&P 500 dropped 4% in one day due to algorithmic trading errors
June 2023 data breach at XYZ Corp exposed 2M customer records via SQL injection
February 2024 supply chain disruption in Asia affected 15% of global semiconductor production

suggested_audits.description: Explicit audit procedures recommended for this risk, distinct from general recommendations.

examples: Annual penetration testing of customer-facing systems
Quarterly review of firewall configuration logs
Monthly assessment of vendor security certifications

contextual_variations.description: How the risk varies by region, industry, company size, or other categories.

examples: More severe in emerging markets due to less mature regulatory frameworks
Highest impact in financial services (8/10) vs. manufacturing (4/10)
Small companies face 3x higher likelihood due to limited security resources
